implementation_notes: cats supplies the contravariant half: Contravariant[F].contramap (instances are documented for Show and scala.math.Ordering), ContravariantSemigroupal, and ContravariantMonoidal whose trivial is conquer and whose contramap2 is cats' encoding of divide - the class documentation cites Kmett's Data.Functor.Contravariant.Divisible. The accumulating verdict comes from Validated/ValidatedNel (Valid/Invalid), whose Apply instance combines errors with a Semigroup instead of short-circuiting. cats has no Decidable class, so sum dispatch (choose) is a hand-written match/Either split or scalaz's Decidable (second variant).
code_sketch:
import cats.syntax.all._

type Err = String
def nonEmpty(s: String): ValidatedNel[Err, String] = Validated.condNel(s.nonEmpty, s, "empty")
def validPort(p: Int): ValidatedNel[Err, Int] = Validated.condNel(p > 0 && p < 65536, p, "port")

case class Config(host: String, port: Int)
val parse: Config => ValidatedNel[Err, Config] = c =>
  (nonEmpty(c.host), validPort(c.port)).mapN(Config.apply)   // divide, all errors kept
pitfalls: Accumulation only survives while the code stays on Apply: switching the same rule set to a for-comprehension or flatMap silently turns it into fail-fast Either semantics and drops the remaining errors.
ValidatedNel needs a Semigroup for the error type: with a plain String you get concatenation, so define an error ADT (sealed trait plus NonEmptyList) when messages must stay structured.
contramap needs the syntax import and the instance in scope: a missing cats.syntax/cats.instances import turns a correct composition into a confusing missing-instance error.

variants.name: scalaz Divisible/Decidable typeclasses (the literal names)
variants.implementation_notes: scalaz carries the literal typeclass names: Divisible[F] extends Divide[F] and adds conquer, documented as the contravariant analogue of scalaz.Applicative; Decidable[F] extends Divisible[F] and adds choose, choose1 and choose2 for sum dispatch - the Scala counterpart of Data.Functor.Contravariant.Divisible, which its own source cites by URL. Choose it when rules must be abstracted over the validator functor (building a rule set for a new carrier, or generic code that consumes F[_]) and when choose-style dispatch belongs in the same typeclass; for ordinary payload validation the cats + Validated variant composes with less ceremony.
pitfalls: scalaz's \/ is not Either: mixing scalaz typeclasses with Either-based code in the same file needs conversions, and the laws you think you are exercising belong to the other library.
The typeclass encodings use Scala 2 implicits; in Scala 3 sources they must be imported in the legacy style, otherwise the Divisible/Decidable instances simply are not in scope.

variants.name: iron refined types (Scala 3)
variants.idiom_name: Refined types: T :| Constraint with refineEither / refineUnsafe
variants.implementation_notes: iron attaches constraint evidence to the type itself: T :| Constraint is used like the underlying type and is checked at compile time for literals and at the boundary via refineEither/option/assert for runtime input - the README's framing is 'attach constraints/assertions to types, to enforce properties and forbid invalid values'. Composition happens through constraint intersection and given instances rather than runtime combinators, which removes the need to re-validate: once you hold a Port, it is a port. Use it when the constraint is stable and belongs to the domain model; keep the runtime-combinator variants when rules change per request or come from configuration.
variants.code_sketch:
import io.github.iltotore.iron.*
import io.github.iltotore.iron.constraint.numeric.*

type Port = Int :| (Greater[0] & Less[65536])

def parsePort(raw: Int): Either[String, Port] = raw.refineEither   // boundary check
val p: Port = 8080                                                 // compile-time verified literal
pitfalls: assert/refineUnsafe throw on violation: at a boundary prefer refineEither/option so the failure accumulates with the other field errors instead of aborting the request.
Every construction in a checked position must find the Constraint given in scope; a missing import produces a compile error naming the constraint rather than your call site.
